places.name: Kota Tua
places.description: Jakarta's old Dutch colonial quarter. Fatahillah Square is ringed by 18th-century warehouses turned into museums, galleries, and street-side cafés — the best-preserved colonial core in Southeast Asia.
highlights: Museum Sejarah Jakarta, the former Batavia town hall (1710)
Historic harbour warehouses along Sunda Kelapa
Café Batavia overlooking the square, serving since 1805
Ondel-ondel puppet performances on weekends

places.name: Bundaran HI
places.description: The pulsing heart of Jakarta's CBD. The Welcome Monument roundabout is flanked by Indonesia's tallest skyscrapers along a 4km corridor stretching south to Senayan.
highlights: Welcome Monument — Jakarta's most iconic landmark
Menara BCA and Pacific Place tower cluster
Car-Free Day every Sunday morning on 26km of pedestrian roads
Grand Indonesia and Plaza Indonesia connected by a sky bridge

places.name: Kemang
places.description: Jakarta's most cosmopolitan neighbourhood — a dense grid of boutique restaurants, rooftop bars, art galleries, and independent boutiques favoured by expats and creative locals.
highlights: Jalan Kemang Raya's 2km strip of restaurants and bars
Rooftop cocktail venues overlooking South Jakarta
Independent fashion boutiques and design studios
Weekend Kemang Timur flea market

places.name: Menteng
places.description: Jakarta's original Dutch colonial residential suburb. Wide tree-lined avenues lead to Taman Suropati at its centre — the most elegant park in the city.
highlights: Taman Suropati, Jakarta's finest colonial public garden
Art deco embassies and ministerial residences
Barack Obama's childhood neighbourhood
Jalan Diponegoro antiques and heritage row

places.name: Ancol Dreamland
places.description: Jakarta's largest beachfront recreation park — art markets, a full marina, and the city's only direct sea access, just 30 minutes from the CBD.
highlights: Pasar Seni art village with 50+ Indonesian artists' studios
Marina Ancol for weekend boat and yacht departures
Atlantis Water Adventure and Dufan amusement park
Jakarta's longest accessible bay view at sunset

places.name: Glodok — Pecinan
places.description: Jakarta's Chinatown — a labyrinth of covered lanes, traditional medicine shops, temple incense, and night food stalls that hasn't changed since the 1700s.
highlights: Jin De Yuan Temple, Jakarta's oldest Chinese temple (1755)
Petak Sembilan traditional market
Night food market with Hainanese chicken rice and hand-pulled noodles
Electronics and rare hardware quarter
